As the function author, since the author has already checked which records are appropriate
As an anonymous identity with no permissions, filling in results from a cached export
quiz.explain: User-facing retrieval runs as the user so the platform enforces access; broad identities with prompt filtering leak data, and running as the author shows everyone the author's view.

quiz.q: Summaries are generated from documents that carry a marking, and the summaries are about to be published to a wide audience. What should happen?
choices: Publish the summaries freely, since a summary is new text and does not contain the original documents
Ask the model to leave out anything sensitive and publish the summaries without any marking
Apply the marking to the summaries, or exclude marked documents from broad-audience outputs
Publish the summaries but add a note at the bottom asking readers not to share them further
quiz.explain: Outputs derived from marked data inherit its sensitivity, so they carry the marking or the workflow excludes those sources; model judgement and polite notes are not access controls.

days.recap: Run user-facing work as the user and elevated work under least-privilege identities, enforce models, residency and spend with platform controls, keep auditable provenance, and let derived AI outputs inherit their sources' markings.

days.title: Human Review, Responsible AI and Prompt Injection Defence

concepts.heading: Review Proportional to Consequence
concepts.body: Validation and human review scale with the consequence of the action, not with how often it happens. Policy answers may need no review, drafted memos a light review, and payment approvals strict validation plus mandatory human approval. Approvals can be tiered by amount: automatic with validation below a small threshold, one approver above it and dual approval for the largest. Low-consequence approvals can be automated safely with validation rules, caps, sampled human audit, anomaly alerts, idempotent approval Actions and logging.

concepts.heading: Uncertainty Means Stop and Escalate
concepts.body: For a consequential action, uncertainty is a reason to stop, not to act or compromise. An agent facing an ambiguous request, such as a cancellation with an unclear date for an order already in delivery, should decline to execute, state the ambiguity and route the decision to a human with the evidence. Where regulation requires review, the action is gated on a recorded approval by a qualified reviewer: the AI drafts, a review task is created, the decision is stored on the object, and an approval-gated Action carries out the result. Each review decision should be logged with the evidence the reviewer saw, so it can be audited later.

concepts.heading: AI in Decisions About People
concepts.body: When AI touches decisions about people, such as hiring, investigations or prioritizing patients, it assists and humans decide. Outputs should be explainable summaries, flags or recommendations with reasons, and protected attributes and their proxies are excluded from inputs. Fairness is evaluated across groups and monitored in production, the practice and its limits are documented, and affected people have a way to appeal. Agents over personal data run as the asking user, so they read only that user's own records, with no tools that reach other people's data.

concepts.heading: Prompt Injection and Untrusted Content
concepts.body: Any content an agent reads, including documents, emails and fetched web pages, is untrusted data that may contain instructions. The first defence is to remove the capability that makes injection dangerous: a summarizing or question-answering agent gets read-only tools and no way to send data externally, and consequential Actions sit behind separate validation and human approval. Content fetched by tools is isolated in the context, consequential actions are never taken on its basis alone, and fetches are restricted to allow-listed sources enforced inside the tool. Tool interfaces use typed, scope-bound parameters so the model cannot author unsafe queries or reach paths outside an allow-list.

concepts.heading: Layered Controls and Blast Radius
concepts.body: Prompts are a non-enforcing layer: defence against jailbreaks and injection combines hardened instructions with input and output safety checks, narrow scope and tools, least-privilege execution identity, human approval, monitoring and adversarial evaluation. Design agents so that a manipulated agent can only do small, reversible, logged things, with per-object tools, write confirmation and caps on amounts. Track injection resistance with a maintained adversarial suite that runs on every change and gates releases. Document security as a control map per boundary (retrieval permissions, tools and Actions, execution identity, prompts and outputs, human review, monitoring) and review it periodically and on change.

examPoints: When a scenario describes an agent that processes untrusted documents and also holds a powerful tool, prefer removing or narrowing that tool and placing consequential Actions behind validation and approval over adding prompt warnings.
When a scenario involves AI flags or rankings about people, prefer explainable recommendations with a human decision, fairness evaluation and an appeal path over automated customer-impacting action.

quiz.q: A question-answering agent over customer emails also has a tool that sends email externally, and testers made it forward data through an injected instruction. What is the best first fix?
choices: Remove or narrow the email-sending tool, routing any legitimate send through a restricted Action
Add a sentence to the instructions telling the agent never to follow instructions found in emails
Switch to a larger model that is better at recognising malicious instructions in content
Block a list of known attack phrases from reaching the agent's context
quiz.explain: Against injection, first remove the capability that makes it dangerous; prompt wording, bigger models and phrase lists are weaker, non-enforcing layers.

quiz.q: An agent may approve expense claims. Which control design matches responsible practice?
choices: The same single approval step for every claim, so that reviewers are not overwhelmed by tiers
Fully automatic approval of every claim, with a monthly report for finance to review afterwards
Tiered review: automatic with validation below a small amount, one approver above it, dual approval for the largest, all logged
Human approval of every claim of any amount, with the agent only able to suggest a decision
quiz.explain: Control scales with consequence: small claims can be automated with validation and logging, larger ones need approvers. Uniform or fully automatic designs ignore consequence, and reviewing everything wastes review capacity.

days.recap: Scale review with consequence, stop and escalate under uncertainty, keep humans in decisions about people, and defend against injection by limiting capability and layering enforced controls.

days.title: Final Review: Cross-Domain Judgement and Exam-Day Strategy

concepts.heading: Know the Exam's Shape
concepts.body: The Palantir AI Engineer – Associate exam is a timed, open-book, multiple-choice exam with 95 questions in 3 hours and a pass mark of 70% correct, covering eight domains. Palantir does not publish domain weights, so this guide and the practice bank treat all eight equally and you should not skip any domain. Three hours for 95 questions is a little under two minutes each, which leaves room to read scenarios carefully but not to look everything up. Open-book helps with confirming a term, not with learning a topic from scratch, so arrive with the judgement patterns already familiar. Certificates are valid for two years, and after a failed attempt there is a 14-day wait before retaking.

concepts.heading: The Recurring Judgement Patterns
concepts.body: Across domains the exam rewards the simplest safe option supported by evidence. Diagnose before you rebuild: read traces, compare with the last good version, and measure retrieval and generation separately. Enforce with platform controls rather than prompt text: withhold tools, run as the user, apply markings, georestrictions and Action validation. Measure before you change: evaluation suites with repeated runs, per-segment results and calibrated graders decide between prompts, models and designs. Ship through versions, pilots and staged rollouts with rollback ready.

concepts.heading: Distractors to Recognise
concepts.body: Wrong answers tend to share a few shapes: switch to a bigger model, write a longer prompt, retrieve or inject more context, raise the temperature, rebuild in code, grant broad access, filter silently, or overwrite production directly. Another family moves the answer outside the AI engineer's role, such as training a custom foundation model when retrieval or prompting solves the problem. When two options both sound reasonable, prefer the one that finds the cause, keeps a guard in place and can be verified with evaluation or traces. Options that sound decisive but skip measurement, such as publishing a fix to every consumer at once, are usually traps.

concepts.heading: Confusable Pairs to Review
concepts.body: Use your error log from practice questions to revisit the pairs that cost the most points. Common ones are: AIP Assist versus a standard agent, embedded versus standalone deployment, south versus north of the Ontology, Pipeline Builder versus Code Repositories transforms for batch AI, deterministic evaluators versus model graders, regression versus run-to-run variance, executing as the user versus a configured identity, and recall versus precision in retrieval. For each pair, be able to state the deciding question in one sentence, such as 'does this depend on the current user's context?'. Rework the practice questions you missed in those areas rather than rereading whole days.

concepts.heading: Pacing and Mindset on the Day
concepts.body: Read the last sentence of each scenario first so you know what is being asked, such as the first step, the best design or the most likely cause. Then pick out the constraints that eliminate options: consequence, permissions, scale, freshness, latency or residency. Words like 'first' usually point to diagnosis over a fix, and 'most consequential' usually points to validation plus human approval. Keep an eye on the clock at regular checkpoints and avoid spending many minutes on a single question.

examPoints: When a scenario offers both a quick capability upgrade (bigger model, longer prompt, more context) and an evidence-driven step (traces, evaluation, filters), prefer the evidence-driven step unless the scenario shows it was already done.
When a scenario's correct-sounding option relies on the model obeying an instruction to stay safe, prefer the option that enforces the rule with permissions, tool scope, validation or approval.

quiz.q: Which principle best describes how to choose between two plausible answers on this exam?
choices: Choose the option that uses the most capable model, since quality is the top priority in AI work
Choose the option that adds the most context, since grounded answers need as much evidence as possible
Choose the simplest safe option that finds the cause or enforces the rule and can be verified
Choose the option that rebuilds the workflow from scratch, since that removes any hidden defects
quiz.explain: The exam rewards evidence-driven, enforceable and verifiable choices; bigger models, more context and rebuilds are classic distractors.

quiz.q: A scenario asks for the first thing to do after an AI workflow's outputs suddenly worsen. Which kind of option is usually right?
choices: Republish the workflow with a new model so that consumers immediately receive a fresh version
A diagnostic step such as reading traces against the last good version while consumers stay on it
Widen the workflow's data access so it can draw on more sources while the cause is investigated
Disable all validation temporarily so that more outputs reach consumers during the incident
quiz.explain: 'First' points to diagnosis that protects consumers; untested republishing, broader access and weaker validation all add risk without finding the cause.

days.recap: Know the exam's shape, apply the recurring patterns (diagnose first, enforce with controls, measure before changing, ship through versions), and recognise the bigger-model, more-context and broad-access distractors.
